solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hot food for this person at start of lunch sitting by idiot

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself, so 'me'

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: an oaf is a clumsy fool

explanation.surface: The setter sits down at lunch beside a fool and orders something hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A baked loaf of minced beef is a dish usually served warm, so it counts as hot food.

clue.text: Confusion which gets them upset — and cat upset too

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads upward

parts.note: 'em is the clipped form of them

indicators.note: again upset turns the cat word upside down

parts.note: puss is a cat

explanation.surface: A muddle that unsettles people, and distresses the cat as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns EM into ME and PUSS into SSUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A muddle or blunder is a mix-up, a state of confusion.

clue.text: I'm Italian priest, working against old-style domination?

indicators.note: working means being worked on, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: the letters of I'm without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An Italian cleric declaring himself an opponent of colonial rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposition to empire-building and colonial rule over other nations is old-style domination resisted.

clue.text: Plant goin' into coiled shape by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase tells the solver to say the words aloud

parts.note: looping, clipped to loopin', is going into a coil

explanation.surface: A climbing plant twisting its tendrils into spirals.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden flower with tall spikes of pea-like blooms.

clue.text: Timeless piece of writing about university — something "hearty"?

indicators.note: about means around, so the shortened word surrounds the university letter
less the letter for time, which is removed

parts.note: an article is a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A timeless essay about college life with plenty of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' takes T from ARTICLE, leaving ARICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An auricle is an atrium, a chamber of the heart, so the quotation marks flag a playful sense.

clue.text: Not just one of a pair taking endless time and trouble

parts.words: Not just one of a pair
parts.note: both of two, rather than one alone

indicators.note: the last letter is cut from the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling that handling two things at once takes forever and causes difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the final A from ERA, leaving ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: bother and trouble both mean fuss or inconvenience.

clue.text: Evident I will get embarrassed and excessively weary

parts.note: overt means plain to see
red, as in blushing

explanation.surface: Clearly someone blushing and worn out from exhaustion.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtired means exhausted beyond the normal point of fatigue.

clue.text: He, as any deceiver, will be unreliable, giving second-hand account

indicators.note: unreliable suggests untrustworthy, so the letters cannot be taken in their order

explanation.surface: A warning that a liar, like any cheat, will tell untrustworthy tales.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands as written at the front; 'unreliable' rearranges AS ANY DECEIVER into ARSAYEVIDENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony repeating what a witness heard from someone else, not first-hand knowledge.

clue.text: Anger about charge going up in the fashion business

indicators.note: about means around, so the anger word surrounds the reversed charge

parts.note: rage is anger

indicators.note: going up in a down clue reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: to dart is to dash or charge

explanation.surface: Fury at prices rising in the clothing industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns DART into TRAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The rag trade is an informal term for the clothing and fashion industry.

clue.text: Turning heads with skill, as one not with the common herd?

definitions.text: as one not with the common herd?

indicators.note: turning round, so the word for heads is read backwards

parts.note: pates are heads
art is skill or craft

explanation.surface: Someone whose clever head-turning style marks them out from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' makes SETAP from PATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone distinguished or separated from ordinary people is described with this phrase.

clue.text: Article that's no good by author in Far East location

parts.note: pen is used for writer, as in 'pen name'
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A worthless piece by a writer set somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Pen as writer comes from phrases like 'pen name' and 'poison pen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Penang is a Malaysian island state, a place in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Illusion of S. American people

definitions.meaning: in Hindu thought, ... is the illusory world of appearances
the ... people of Central America and southern Mexico

explanation.surface: A Latin American tribe as a mere mirage.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both the Hindu concept of cosmic illusion and an ancient Mesoamerican civilization.

clue.text: Group of workers? A particular one puts Society off

indicators.note: puts off means removes, so the letter for Society is taken away

parts.note: Unison is a large British public-sector trade ...

explanation.surface: A trade body that alienates the Society by its conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: UNISON is a big UK public service union; removing S gives the general word.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade association of employees banding together is the standard sense here.

clue.text: One severely scolding a naughty sister after church

indicators.note: the anagram comes after the church abbreviation
naughty suggests misbehaving, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stern figure tells off a misbehaving nun after the service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' rearranges A SISTER into ASTISER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rebukes or punishes harshly is a castigator, the agent noun of chastise.

clue.text: Track in Home Counties reveals something botanical

indicators.note: the track word goes inside the region's letters

parts.note: the Home Counties are the counties around London, in the South East (SE) of England
a path is a track

explanation.surface: A footpath in the countryside near London turns up a plant feature.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, hence SE for South East.
explanation.definitionFit: A spathe is a large bract enclosing a flower spike, a plant structure.

clue.text: Exam on biblical word that's first seen in group of holy books

parts.note: a test is an exam
amen closes prayers in the Bible

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A test about the Bible's opening words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old and New Testaments are each a collection of scriptural books.

clue.text: Laid out report of an aggressive act

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: a raid is an aggressive attack

explanation.surface: A news report of an attack, describing what was set out.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrayed means arranged or set out in order, as troops or goods are laid out.

clue.text: Naughty rascal turning up in that monastic garb

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the anagram
naughty suggests misbehaving, so the letters are mixed
turning round means read backwards

explanation.surface: A mischievous rogue twists into a monk's habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' makes SCALAR from RASCAL; 'turning' makes PU from UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapular is a sleeveless outer garment worn by monks over their habit.

clue.text: Certainly taken aback by abrupt gesture of respect

indicators.note: the reversed word sits beside the word for abrupt

parts.note: curt means abrupt or brusque

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the word for certainly is reversed

parts.note: yes means certainly

explanation.surface: Someone startled by a brusque bow, though it was meant respectfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' turns YES into SEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob or bending of the knee, made by women, shows deference.

clue.text: There's still one needing to be found

definitions.text: There's still one needing to be found

parts.note: yet means still
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Something remains undiscovered.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the Himalayan creature, whose existence is unproven.
explanation.definitionFit: The Abominable Snowman has never been confirmed, so searchers still seek proof.

clue.text: Travel with dominant female, one making notorious journey on horseback

definitions.text: one making notorious journey on horseback

parts.note: to go is to travel
a diva is a prima donna, a dominating woman

explanation.surface: Setting off with a strong-willed woman, famed for a scandalous ride.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Godiva, legend says, rode naked through Coventry.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval noblewoman famously rode unclothed through Coventry streets on a horse.

clue.text: Awful grief comes with the trapping of a fine animal

indicators.note: trapping means enclosing, so the anagram holds the other letters
awful suggests a mess, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Terrible sorrow over a fine animal being caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges GRIEF into GIRFE, which traps A F.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-necked African creature is an example of a mammal.

clue.text: Show butcher's ultimate English meat

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so the last letter is taken

parts.note: veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: A butcher's finest English meat on display.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal and to show both mean to make visible or disclose.

clue.text: Agreement by men to accommodate amateur performer who hams it up?

indicators.note: accommodating something means housing it, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: a pact is an agreement
lay means non-professional
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A deal between troops to take on a theatrical amateur.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is the crossword staple for men.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who overacts and exaggerates feeling, sometimes off-stage, fits this description.

clue.text: Fighting unit in trouble when duke intervenes

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so the duke's letter goes inside

parts.note: care means worry or trouble

explanation.surface: A military squad in difficulties until a nobleman steps in.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a core group of trained soldiers or activists forming a unit.

clue.text: Small child unwell — on account if this?

definitions.text: Small child unwell — on account if this?

parts.note: CH is a short form of child
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A little one might be poorly because of a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue suggests a common cause of a child falling sick.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold or feverish shivering is a typical reason for being poorly.

clue.text: Icelander managed without car in the city

indicators.note: managed signals rearranging, and without signals taking the letters of car away from the pool

explanation.surface: A Nordic visitor got by in town without a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C, A, R from ICELANDER and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Leiden is a Dutch university city in South Holland.

clue.text: A loud female that is holding party in Africa to get engaged

parts.note: F is forte, the musical abbreviation for loud

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the party goes inside

parts.note: IE is id est, that is
the ANC is South Africa's African National Congress

explanation.surface: A noisy woman involved with an African party plans her wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: IE (that is) holds ANC to give IANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Affiance means to betroth, to pledge to marry.

clue.text: Rubbish written by troublemaker makes one reel

parts.note: rot is nonsense
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Nonsense written by a stirrer sends someone into a spin.
explanation.walkthrough: Ate is the Greek goddess of folly and mischief, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel can mean to spin round, turning on an axis.

clue.text: Measure introduced by prime minister, that measure creating disorder

indicators.note: the measure is put in among the letters of the prime minister

parts.note: an ell is an old length measure
the same old length measure again

explanation.surface: A government policy brought in by the premier causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: An ell is an old cloth measure of about 45 inches.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, used as a noun, means confused haste or jumble, a state of chaos.
